title: Let The People Set The Pace Of Frontier AI | NOEMA
gist: Landemore and Tang argue the US-China and inter-lab frontier AI race is a nested stag hunt (not a prisoner's dilemma) solvable via an assurance mechanism: lab-permitted independent evaluators plus a standing, lottery-selected 1,000-person Global Citizens' Assembly on AI whose recommendations labs and governments must publicly answer, with the EU AI Office code of practice as the first legal anchor. They propose labs pilot 5-20% compute safety budgets and seat a first cohort by spring 2027.

insights.claim: On Sept. 12 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing the pace of AI model improvement and committed to giving independent third-party evaluators ongoing employee-like access; OpenAI's Sam Altman matched the pledge within hours and Elon Musk endorsed it.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Frontier lab leaders publicly converging on self-imposed pacing signals possible slower capability cadence and new compliance/evaluation overhead.
insights.quote: Within hours, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman agreed that “we need to pace the frontier” and made the same evaluator pledge. Elon Musk’s response was three words: “Dario is right.”

insights.claim: More than 1,300 employees at leading AI companies have called on Washington to back an international AI slowdown, amid models circumventing safeguards and researchers departing labs over catastrophic-risk disagreements.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Internal labor pressure inside labs is a growing driver of policy and talent risk for AI companies.
insights.quote: more than 1,300 employees at leading AI companies have called on Washington to back an international slowdown
insights.locator: This apparent convergence among the leaders

insights.claim: CEO agreement alone cannot stop the race because Washington and Beijing each fear that restraint hands strategic advantage to the other.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Voluntary lab pacing is unlikely to translate into actual slowdown without a US-China assurance mechanism; investors shouldn't price a real deceleration yet.
insights.quote: But even if the CEOs agree, the race does not stop.

insights.claim: Anthropic has committed to letting embedded evaluators publish without its editorial control, and OpenAI promised to follow.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Externally published evaluator findings could become market-moving disclosures for lab valuations and IPO narratives.
insights.quote: Anthropic has committed to letting embedded evaluators publish without its editorial control, and OpenAI has promised to follow.

insights.claim: The frontier AI race is a double nested collective-action problem: the inter-lab domestic race and the US-China race, where 'If we slow down, China wins' is the main argument against binding regulation.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Any US-China détente on AI would remove the main political cover against domestic regulation of labs.
insights.quote: The outer race is the inner one’s best excuse; end the global race, and the domestic one loses cover.
insights.locator: What we are facing, in other words

insights.claim: Both races resemble a stag hunt rather than a prisoner's dilemma: every player prefers a shared slowdown and defects only from lack of trust, so the remedy is an assurance mechanism rather than coercion or a global regulatory leviathan.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: If correct, cooperative pacing equilibria are reachable with verification, making coordinated slowdown scenarios more plausible than consensus assumes.
insights.quote: The way out of a stag hunt is not coercion but an assurance mechanism.
insights.locator: The way out of a stag hunt

insights.claim: Assurance requires both verification and a witness credible to all parties; evaluators hired by labs and judging against lab-defined thresholds cannot reassure rival labs or governments.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Current lab-controlled safety evaluations have limited credibility value; demand may grow for independent, standard-setting verifiers.
insights.quote: Evidence changes what the hunters believe about one another only when it flows to someone none of them controls, and who has set the standard it is measured against.
insights.locator: The first is already taking shape.

insights.claim: The UN is unsuitable as the AI-race referee because the Security Council gives Washington and Beijing each a veto and the institution speaks only for sovereign states.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Don't expect UN-led AI governance to bind the US or China.
insights.quote: The Security Council grants Washington and Beijing each a veto over the institution meant to referee them.
insights.locator: The obvious candidate is the United Nations

insights.claim: The authors propose a standing Global Citizens' Assembly on AI of 1,000 people chosen by lot worldwide, sitting continuously with part-time terms and a third of seats regularly redrawn, to set AI's purposes and limits and receive evaluators' findings.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: A new deliberative governance node could become a reputational pressure point on lab behavior and product limits.
insights.locator: Our proposal is a standing global

insights.claim: The 1,000-member size is chosen for symbolism and salience rather than statistical representativeness, so that a lab leader refusing to answer it must refuse publicly on the planetary stage.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Governance designed to maximize reputational cost of non-compliance raises headline risk for labs that ignore it.
insights.quote: A CEO can shrug off a critic, even a panel of experts.

insights.claim: A 'duty to answer' is central: each assembly recommendation goes to a named lab or government with a deadline to publicly accept or reject with reasons, fixed in advance by law or enforceable agreement.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Mandatory public response obligations would add disclosure and legal-risk burdens for frontier labs.
insights.quote: Law or enforceable agreement would fix the obligation in advance, as an invitation to advise means nothing when the recipient can ignore it.
insights.locator: The duty to answer, in particular

insights.claim: An independent civic secretariat would pool disclosed funding from governments and labs while insulating recruitment and evidence from funders; AI tools would handle translation and summarization, with members able to reject the machine's account.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Creates potential demand for AI-assisted deliberation and translation tooling.

insights.claim: Over 800 deliberative bodies like the proposed one have been convened worldwide per the OECD, including the 100-person Global Assembly for COP26, Meta's 6,300-person Metaverse Community Forum across 32 countries, Anthropic and CIP's ~1,000-American constitution exercise, and Taiwan's 2024 process texting 200,000 numbers to seat 447 people.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Deliberative AI governance has real precedents and could scale, informing regulatory trajectory.
insights.quote: More than 800 deliberative bodies similar to the one we propose have been convened around the world, according to the OECD.

insights.claim: If started now, a first assembly cohort could be seated by spring and deliberate through the rest of 2027.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Sets a concrete timeline to watch for an AI governance body forming in 2027.
insights.quote: If we start today, a first cohort can be seated by spring and deliberating through the rest of 2027.

themes.theme: EU AI Office as legal anchor

insights.claim: Since August, the EU AI Office can fine frontier-model providers or order mitigations or recalls, and Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI have all signed the safety and security chapter of the code of practice.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: EU enforcement powers over frontier models (fines, recalls) are now live and apply to all major US labs.
insights.quote: Since August, the EU’s AI Office can fine a frontier-model provider or order mitigations or a recall.
insights.locator: One jurisdiction already has enforcement powers

insights.claim: Under the EU code of practice each lab defines its own risk tiers, judges its own risk acceptability and picks its own evaluators; the public gets only summaries and public consultation ranks last among eight information-gathering methods.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: The EU regime is weaker on independence than headlines suggest; a tightening revision is a policy risk to watch.
insights.quote: The most developed safety regime in law to date still treats the public as an input rather than a party.
insights.locator: But in this system, each lab

insights.claim: A revised EU code of practice clause obliging signatories to publicly answer a global assembly's recommendations would give the duty to answer legal force, because no frontier lab can afford to leave the EU market.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: EU market access is the lever likely to impose new governance obligations on US labs.
insights.quote: in a market no frontier lab can afford to leave
insights.locator: But in this system, each lab

insights.claim: Beijing denounces 'exclusive groups' in AI governance and has built its own frameworks, including the Global AI Governance Initiative and a World AI Cooperation Organization launched this summer in Shanghai.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: China is building parallel AI governance institutions, deepening bloc fragmentation in standards.

insights.claim: A lottery-based global assembly is the least Western-dominated forum available, with roughly one seat in six going to someone living in China, which turns Washington's claim that Beijing would never restrain itself into a testable proposition.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: A credible test of Chinese willingness to pace could shift the US political case against AI regulation.
insights.quote: By population alone, roughly one seat in six would belong to someone living in China.

insights.claim: If labs accept assembly-vetted evaluators and a duty to answer, US restraint becomes a verified conditional offer before a witness rather than a unilateral gift to Beijing.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Shows a pathway by which a US slowdown could become politically viable.
insights.quote: Washington’s restraint would no longer be a unilateral gift to Beijing, but a verified, conditional offer, made before a witness, that Beijing is invited to join.

insights.claim: Participating labs could pilot a transparent safety-research budget of 5% to 20% of their compute under published accounting rules, plus explicit caps on compute used to accelerate capability research.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Compute-based pacing commitments would directly affect capability-research compute demand and GPU allocation at labs.
insights.quote: They could pilot a transparent safety-research budget of 5% to 20% of their compute, under published accounting rules

insights.claim: A separate compute allocation could fund public-use computing with affected communities choosing projects, but no public benefit could be traded for a safety-limit breach.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Public-compute set-asides are a possible new channel of compute demand.

insights.claim: The authors acknowledge critics who argue AI-doom hype merely serves lucrative public offerings, contending the assembly would remain useful for AI, climate, terrorism and migration regardless.
insights.speaker: HÉLÈNE LANDEMORE AND AUDREY TANG
insights.so_what: Signals awareness that lab safety rhetoric is entangled with upcoming IPO narratives.
insights.quote: critics are right that the hype merely serves lucrative public offerings
